content:
Why Punjab and Delhi Universities Are on Edge: Inside the LPU, Chitkara, and DU Protests

Over the last few days, three Indian university campuses have witnessed serious unrest, all connected by one theme: unverified rumours about student safety spreading faster than facts.

Chitkara University: Where It Started

The trouble began at Chitkara University near Rajpura, Punjab, on the night of September 25 into September 26, 2026. Rumours started circulating that two first-year female students had died by suicide, a claim that grew after students said they heard screams from a hostel and noticed two ambulances on the campus. This triggered a large, late-night gathering of angry students demanding answers. 
LatestLY

Students protested and allegedly damaged a police vehicle over these unverified claims, while police said they were conducting an inquiry into the matter. The local DSP later said that the students who raised the alarm couldn't even name the girls they claimed were missing. University registrar Col. Rakesh Sharma (Retd) dismissed the suicide claims as "baseless rumours" and said the campus situation was fine. 
Chitkara University Protest: Students Raise Unverified Claims Of 2 Female Students’ Suicide, Police Vehicle Damaged As Authorities Deny Incident | Video +2

LPU: A Similar Story, Turns Violent

Barely a day later, a much larger and more destructive protest broke out at Lovely Professional University (LPU) in Phagwara, Punjab. Unrest began around 2 a.m. on the night of September 26–27, 2026, near the girls' hostel, after a social media message alleged that a female student had been raped. Students alleged the victim had been assaulted by a plumber three days earlier. 
Wionews
TheQuint

Things escalated quickly. Protesting students smashed window panes, pelted bricks and flower pots, and set parts of buildings on fire. They also blocked the Phagwara–Jalandhar National Highway, disrupting traffic for hours as police were deployed in large numbers. Other rumours claimed an electrician had groped a student, and that the administration was covering it up by pinning it on an outsider — none of which were verified. 
LPU students go on rampage, vandalise campus amid widespread protest: What's happening +2

Kapurthala SP Gaurav Toora said the rape allegation had not been confirmed and that an investigation was underway. LPU rejected several of the circulating claims as false, though the university has also faced scrutiny over a separate, confirmed case: a 21-year-old student died by suicide on campus earlier this month, on September 10, 2026. 
Wionews
The Statesman

Delhi: A Different, More Serious Trigger

The Delhi protests stem from a real and confirmed crime, not a rumour. On September 21, 2026, a 17-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped by three men in Aastha Kunj Park near Kalkaji Mandir, after she and a male friend visited the temple and entered the park. 
Business Standard

What made this worse for nearby students was what happened next. One of the accused, Asif, allegedly opened fire on a police team that intercepted him barely 50 metres from Lady Shri Ram College's (LSR) back gate, firing three rounds — one of which hit a constable's bulletproof vest — before police shot him in the leg. LSR suspended offline classes and shifted sessions online as safety fears grew. 
Business Standard
Business Standard

This led women students to speak up. LSR students held an all-women solidarity march, raising slogans and carrying posters demanding better security infrastructure around the college. They pointed to poor lighting, weak patrolling, missing CCTV coverage, and a non-functional police "pink booth" near the campus, alongside repeated complaints of stalking near the college gate. The LSR Students' Union argued that the responsibility for women's safety cannot rest on women alone. 
LSR Students Stage Solidarity March Over Gang Rape Of Minor Near Aastha Kunj, Demand Women's Safety +2

The Common Thread

What connects Chitkara and LPU is clear: unverified posts on platforms like Instagram and Reddit created panic that boiled over into real violence, before any official confirmation existed. In Delhi's case, the underlying incident was real and confirmed — but it exposed genuine gaps in public safety infrastructure that women students say they've been flagging for years.

For students, parents, and campus administrators, the lesson is the same everywhere: verify before reacting, but also fix the safety gaps that make rumours believable in the first place.

title: CEC Gyanesh Kumar Row: CJP's "Jantar Mantar 2.0" Explained
subtitle: CJP demands CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over voter roll allegations. Know the full timeline, key claims, and the October 2 "Jantar Mantar 2.0" protest plan.
excerpt: Cockroach Janta Party Threatens "Jantar Mantar 2.0" — Will CEC Gyanesh Kumar Resign?
content:
Cockroach Janta Party Threatens "Jantar Mantar 2.0" — Will CEC Gyanesh Kumar Resign?

India's Chief Election Commissioner (CEC), Gyanesh Kumar, is facing one of the biggest controversies of his tenure. The youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has demanded his resignation, and if he refuses, the group says it will launch a fresh nationwide protest movement — one being called "Jantar Mantar 2.0." Here's everything you need to know about how this controversy started, what's being alleged, and whether more protests are actually on the way.

How Did This Controversy Start?

The trouble began after an investigative report by The Indian Express. According to the report, two Election Commissioners — Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi — formally objected or raised concerns at least 14 times over the past 10 months. Their objections were mainly about the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and changes to Form 6, the form used by first-time voters to register.

The dissenting commissioners reportedly said that important decisions — about adding, deleting, or restoring voter names — were being pushed through in the name of the "full commission" without their prior knowledge or proper authorization. Some of these decisions have even been described internally as "unauthorised and illegal." The Election Commission has pushed back on suggestions of any internal rift.

What Did CJP Founder Abhijeet Dipke Say?

At a press conference, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke called Gyanesh Kumar "the biggest threat to India's democracy" and labelled him "anti-national." He alleged that during the SIR process, more than 13 crore (130 million) voters were removed from electoral rolls across major states, including Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Delhi, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and Telangana.

Dipke went further, claiming specific examples: around 50,000 votes deleted from West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee's constituency (where she lost by roughly 15,000 votes), about 100,000 votes deleted in Tamil Nadu CM MK Stalin's constituency, and around 40,000 votes deleted from Arvind Kejriwal's Delhi constituency. He alleged that these deletions were designed to shift regional demographics in a way that benefits the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). It's worth noting these are allegations made by Dipke and CJP — they have not been independently verified or established as fact.

What Does CJP Actually Want?

CJP's co-conveners — Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka, and Abhijeet Dipke — issued a strict 48-hour ultimatum demanding Gyanesh Kumar's immediate resignation. Their broader demands reportedly also include freezing upcoming elections and reversing the recent changes made to the Special Intensive Revision process.

Tension on the Streets of Delhi

Meanwhile, the pressure has already started spilling onto the streets. The All India Students' Association (AISA) organised a quick demonstration at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, where protesters demanded action against the CEC. Delhi Police responded swiftly, and several student protesters — including some organisers — were detained, with police citing the lack of prior administrative permission for the gathering.

Will There Be More Protests?

Yes — and this isn't just speculation. Since the 48-hour deadline passed without a resignation, CJP has already laid out its roadmap for a much bigger movement.

The launch date is October 2, 2026 — Gandhi Jayanti — and the protest will kick off from Mumbai. From there, CJP plans to carry the agitation to other major Indian cities before eventually shifting its base to New Delhi for what's being called an indefinite protest — nicknamed "Jantar Mantar 2.0," a nod to the massive student protests earlier this year that led to the resignation of then-Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

It's important to remember that CJP isn't a registered political party — it started in May 2026 as a satirical, social-media-driven youth movement, born out of a remark comparing unemployed young Indians to "cockroaches." Despite its satirical roots, the group has shown it can mobilise real, large-scale protests.

The Social Media Buzz

Right now, social media is flooded with reels and comments about "Jantar Mantar 2.0," along with viral slang like "it's done, bro." The movement clearly still has strong traction among India's youth, and how the government responds in the coming days could decide whether this turns into another major national flashpoint — just like the protests that forced out Dharmendra Pradhan earlier this year.

What Happens Next?

All eyes are now on October 2. If CJP follows through as promised, India could see another large-scale, youth-driven protest movement — this time targeting the country's top election official rather than a cabinet minister. Whether the Election Commission responds with reforms, clarifications, or silence will likely shape how far this movement goes.

India This Week: Politics, Markets, Sports and the Rise of Gen Z Culture
Political Unrest Over SIR Protests
Delhi Police recently detained several prominent leaders during protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
Activist Yogendra Yadav and AISA (All India Students' Association) president Neha Bora were among those taken into custody.
Neha Bora has been a central figure in student-led movements this year, having earlier led a prolonged hunger strike at Jantar Mantar over exam-related grievances.
The detentions have reignited debate over the SIR exercise, which has already triggered friction in states like West Bengal and Tamil Nadu ahead of upcoming elections.
Stock Market Jolt: PB Fintech Under Pressure
PB Fintech (parent of Policybazaar) has seen sharp volatility in recent sessions, rattling investor confidence.
The trigger: a regulatory push from IRDAI around tightening or restructuring insurance agent commission structures.
Since commissions are a core part of PB Fintech's revenue model, any regulatory tightening directly affects investor sentiment toward the stock.
This adds to a turbulent year for new-age tech stocks, several of which remain sensitive to regulatory and policy signals.
Festive Season Relief: Edible Oil Duties
With festival season approaching, the government has been active in managing edible oil import duties to keep kitchen essentials affordable for households.
This is a recurring policy pattern — the Centre typically adjusts import duties around Diwali and Navratri to control cooking oil prices amid rising festive demand.
Asian Games 2026: The China Challenge
The Asian Games 2026 are currently underway in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan (running mid-September to early October).
China currently leads the medal tally, putting pressure on the Indian contingent to close the gap in the remaining events.
India's early campaign has been strongly powered by shooting and archery, though the competition from China remains intense as the Games progress.
Gen Z's Festive Innovation: "Rent a Garba Partner"
As Navratri approaches, a new Gen Z trend has gone viral: "Rent a Garba Partner."
Instagram ads are offering "Garba Companions" for ₹1,000 to ₹6,500, promising dance lessons, matching outfits, and reel-worthy photo moments.
What started as internet humor took a serious turn after a Mumbai-based politician filed a complaint with Mumbai Police.
The incident sparked a wider generational debate — many argued the older generation misread a playful trend as something scandalous.
Flipkart's Gen Z Gatekeeping Campaign
Flipkart launched its Big Billion Days campaign titled "Are You Really Gen Z?"
The campaign features a dedicated microsite protected by pop-culture and slang-based CAPTCHAs.
The idea plays on generational gatekeeping — testing whether users truly understand Gen Z vocabulary before letting them access trending fashion deals.
Content creators have since turned it into a challenge, posting videos of themselves attempting (and passing) the slang test.
The Slang Takeover: "6-7" and "Aura Farming"
Two terms dominating Indian internet culture right now: "6-7" and "Aura Farming."
"6-7" has become a viral inside joke with no fixed meaning — used purely for comic effect in comment sections.
"Aura Farming" is used by creators to describe someone deliberately projecting an exaggerated "cool" persona online.
The "Cockroach" Movement's Political Ripple Effect
The paper-leak protests (linked to the NEET examination controversy) led to the resignation of the Union Education Minister.
The protest wave, popularly dubbed the "Cockroach Janata Party" movement, became a defining cultural and political moment of the year.
Gen Z slang like "Delulu," "FOMO," and "MIA" made an unusual crossover — even being used by MPs during Lok Sabha debates, showing how internet culture is now shaping formal political discourse.

Meta Quest 3: Specs, Display, Mixed Reality, Battery Life and Price

The Meta Quest 3 is a virtual reality (VR) and mixed reality (MR) headset that Meta launched in October 2023. It is a big upgrade over the Quest 2, with faster performance, sharper visuals and a much better mixed reality experience. In this article, we look at its chipset, display, cameras, audio, battery life and price, so you can decide if it is right for you.

Performance and Chipset

The Quest 3 runs on the Qualcomm Snapdragon XR2 Gen 2 chipset, paired with 8GB of RAM. Meta says this gives the headset almost double the graphics power of the Quest 2. In simple terms, games and apps load faster, frame rates stay smooth, and scenes look more detailed. If you enjoy fast games or large virtual worlds, you will notice the difference quickly.

Display Quality

The headset uses LCD panels with a resolution of 2064 x 2208 pixels per eye. It also uses pancake lenses, which are thinner than the lenses in older headsets. These lenses reduce blur and keep the image clear across a wider part of your view. Text is easier to read, and small details in games and videos look sharper. The clarity feels close to a very high-resolution screen held right in front of you, even though it is not literally a 4K monitor.

Mixed Reality Cameras and Sensors

The front of the headset has vertical sensor clusters that make mixed reality possible. It includes two 4-megapixel RGB cameras that capture your surroundings in full colour with a stereoscopic view. This feature is called passthrough. It lets you see your real room clearly while digital objects appear on top of it.

The central cluster also holds an infrared depth sensor. This sensor scans your space and maps walls, furniture and other objects. Because of this, virtual items can sit on your real table or react to your real walls in a believable way. It makes the Quest 3 useful for fitness, creative work and everyday apps, not just games.

Audio Experience

The built-in stereo speakers sit on the headstrap. Meta says they are about 40% louder than the speakers in the previous model. They offer 3D spatial audio, strong bass and clear directional sound, so you can tell where a sound is coming from in a game. If you prefer wired audio, there is also a 3.5mm headphone jack.

Battery Life and Connectivity

Battery life is average. Meta says it lasts around 2.2 hours, and heavy gaming may drain it faster. Charging is done through a USB Type-C port. For wireless connections, the headset supports Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.2, which help with fast downloads, stable streaming and smooth connections to controllers and accessories. If you plan long sessions, a battery strap or a power bank can help.

Price

In India, the Quest 3 has been sold at roughly ₹58,999 to ₹73,999, $499.99 (128GB) / $649.99 (512GB) depending on the storage model and offers. Prices change often, so always check the official Meta store or a trusted retailer before buying.

Pros and Cons

Pros

Strong performance from the Snapdragon XR2 Gen 2 chipset
Sharp display with clear pancake lenses
Colour passthrough for good mixed reality
Louder, better spatial audio
Wireless, standalone use with no PC required

Cons

Battery life of about 2.2 hours is short
Price is high for casual users
Can feel heavy during long sessions
Who Should Buy the Meta Quest 3?

The Quest 3 suits gamers who want smooth graphics, fitness fans who like active VR workouts, and anyone curious about mixed reality. If you already own a Quest 2, the jump in clarity, speed and passthrough quality is worth considering. If you only want to try VR occasionally, a cheaper headset may be a better choice.

Final Verdict

The Meta Quest 3 is one of the most complete standalone headsets available. Its powerful chipset, sharp lenses and colour mixed reality cameras make it a real step forward. Battery life and price are the main drawbacks, but for most enthusiasts the experience is worth it.

Canon PowerShot G7 X Mark III: Is It Still Worth Buying in 2026?
Meta Title

Canon PowerShot G7 X Mark III Review 2026: Still Worth Buying?

The Canon PowerShot G7 X Mark III launched back in August 2019, and it quickly became the go-to camera for photographers and vloggers who wanted a serious 1-inch sensor camera that could still fit in a jacket pocket. Seven years on, you'd expect it to have faded into obsolescence. Instead, it has done the opposite — the G7 X Mark III is currently one of the most in-demand compact cameras on the planet, driven largely by its continued popularity with content creators on YouTube and TikTok. Stock shortages are common, and resale prices often run well above the original launch price. So the real question in 2026 isn't whether this camera was good — it's whether it still makes sense to buy one today.

Specifications That Still Hold Up

At its core, the G7 X Mark III uses a 20.1MP 1-inch stacked CMOS sensor paired with Canon's DIGIC 8 processor. This combination was ahead of its time in 2019 and remains genuinely competent even now, delivering clean, detailed images with minimal noise even in moderately low light.

The lens covers a 24-100mm equivalent range with 4.2x optical zoom, and a bright f/1.8-2.8 aperture that helps with both low-light shooting and background separation. The 3-inch touchscreen tilts a full 180 degrees, which is exactly what vloggers need for framing selfie-style shots. On the connectivity side, you get Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, USB-C charging, and a 3.5mm external microphone input — a rare and valuable inclusion at this size and price point.

One correction worth making here: contrary to some claims floating around, the G7 X Mark III can live stream directly to YouTube. This was actually one of its standout launch features back in 2019, and it still works over Wi-Fi paired with a smartphone.

Real-World Performance

The 1-inch sensor is what really sets this camera apart from smartphone cameras, even today's flagship phones. Canon's color science tends to render skin tones warmly and naturally, and the sensor size gives images noticeably better dynamic range and subject separation than what a phone camera can typically produce.

For stills, the f/1.8-2.8 lens allows for pleasing background blur on portraits, while still being versatile enough for wider shots. For video, this camera remains a strong choice for creators — it can record 4K video without any crop, which was unusual for a compact camera in this class when it launched and still holds value today. Combined with the flip screen and the mic input, it's easy to see why vloggers have stuck with it for so long.

At roughly 304 grams, it's genuinely pocketable, which is a big part of the appeal for creators who want a "grab and go" camera rather than a bulky DSLR or mirrorless setup.

Where It Falls Short

No camera is perfect, and the G7 X Mark III does show its age in a few areas. Battery life is on the weaker side — you're looking at around 235 to 265 shots per charge in standard use, and 4K video recording drains the battery considerably faster. Heavy 4K shooting can also cause the camera to run warm, which some users have reported affecting extended recording sessions.

Autofocus is another area where the Mark III shows its years — it's reliable in good light but can hunt a bit in trickier conditions compared to newer cameras with more advanced tracking systems.

Price and Availability in 2026

Here's where things get interesting. The original launch price was around ₹99,995 (roughly $749.99), but because demand has stayed unusually high for a camera this old, actual market prices have been all over the place — some retailers list it closer to ₹70,000, while limited-stock situations have pushed prices as high as ₹2 lakh or more in certain listings. If you're shopping for one, it's worth comparing prices across a few trusted retailers rather than assuming a single "market rate," since availability shifts frequently.

What's Coming Next

If you're on the fence, it's worth knowing that Canon is reportedly working on a true successor. Rumors point to a 2026 launch, possibly not even carrying the "Mark IV" name, with an upgraded sensor, better low-light performance, and improved video capabilities. Canon has publicly acknowledged that a new compact camera with "new technology" is in development. If you can wait, a newer model may be worth holding out for — but there's no confirmed release date yet, so it could still be a while.

Final Verdict

So, is the Canon PowerShot G7 X Mark III still worth the hype in 2026? For most photographers and vloggers who want a compact, capable camera right now, yes — its sensor quality, video features, and portability still hold up well against the competition, including many smartphones. The battery life and aging autofocus are real trade-offs, but they haven't stopped it from remaining one of the most sought-after compact cameras years after launch. If a successor is genuinely important to you and you can wait, it might be worth watching for updates through 2026. But if you need a reliable creator camera today, the G7 X Mark III still earns its reputation.

Avengers: Doomsday Release Date, Cast, and Everything You Need to Know

The wait for Marvel's next big crossover event is almost over. Avengers: Doomsday is confirmed to release in cinemas worldwide on December 18, 2026, and the buzz around it has only grown stronger with every new update. From a returning Marvel legend playing a brand-new villain to one of the biggest ensemble casts in movie history, here's a complete breakdown of everything confirmed so far.

Release Date

Marvel has locked in December 18, 2026 as the global release date for Avengers: Doomsday. Interestingly, this date puts the film on a direct collision course with two other major releases hitting theaters the very same day, making it one of the most competitive box-office weekends in recent memory.

Who Is Directing Avengers: Doomsday?

The film is being directed by Joe Russo and Anthony Russo, popularly known as the Russo Brothers. Fans will remember them as the directing duo behind two of the biggest MCU films ever made, Avengers: Infinity War and Avengers: Endgame. Their return to the franchise has already built massive expectations, since they have a strong track record of handling large ensemble casts and high-stakes storytelling.

Who Wrote the Screenplay?

The screenplay duties are being handled by Stephen McFeely, a writer closely associated with some of the MCU's most successful films. His experience with large-scale Marvel storytelling makes him a fitting choice for a project of this scale.

The Big Villain: Robert Downey Jr. as Doctor Doom

Perhaps the most talked-about update is the casting of Robert Downey Jr., who fans have loved for years as Iron Man, now returning to the MCU in a completely different role: Doctor Doom. This marks one of the boldest casting decisions in recent Marvel history, as Downey Jr. steps away from his iconic hero role to play the franchise's central villain.

Star-Studded Cast Lineup

Avengers: Doomsday brings together one of the largest casts ever assembled for a superhero film. Some of the confirmed names include:

Chris Hemsworth as Thor
Tom Holland
Florence Pugh
Sebastian Stan

The film also introduces the new Fantastic Four cast, joining the MCU for the first time in this crossover:

Pedro Pascal

Adding even more star power, two legendary X-Men actors are also set to appear:

Patrick Stewart as Professor X
Ian McKellen as Magneto

This combination of Avengers, Fantastic Four, and X-Men characters sharing the same screen is being seen as a historic moment for Marvel fans.

What Are the Plot Leaks Saying?

While Marvel hasn't officially revealed the full story, a few rumors have been circulating online:

Doctor Doom approaches the Fantastic Four at the Baxter Building, warning them about a massive threat that needs to be stopped urgently.
Doctor Doom is said to be seeking help from Reed Richards to investigate a mysterious multiversal anomaly.
Reports suggest the film may open with an explosive multiverse-collision sequence, potentially showing different universes and past franchise realities crashing into one another.

It's worth remembering these are unconfirmed leaks, so the actual story details will only be clear once the film releases.

From Kang to Doom: A Behind-the-Scenes Shift

Originally, this project was planned around the villain Kang the Conqueror. However, Marvel reportedly restructured the film and shifted the story to center around Doctor Doom instead. This decision came after certain complications during the writing phase involving the actor originally cast as Kang. Marvel also built anticipation for the film by launching an official countdown in August 2026, which included an Avengers: Doomsday podcast hosted by Iman Vellani.

Box Office Clash: Dune Part 3 and King

The December 18, 2026 release date sets up a major box-office showdown. Avengers: Doomsday is expected to clash with Dune: Part Three and Shah Rukh Khan's much-anticipated film King, making it one of the most competitive release weekends of the year.

Final Thoughts

With a legendary director duo, a script from an experienced Marvel writer, and possibly the biggest cast in MCU history, Avengers: Doomsday is shaping up to be one of the most ambitious superhero films ever made. As more official details and trailers arrive, fans can expect even bigger surprises before its December 18, 2026 release.

content:
ASUS ROG G16 (2026): Zephyrus G16 vs Strix G16 — Which One Should You Actually Buy?

ASUS has two very different laptops sharing almost the same name. The ROG Zephyrus G16 and the ROG Strix G16 are both 16-inch gaming machines, both carry the ROG badge, and both cost serious money. But they are built for two completely different kinds of people, and once you understand that split, choosing between them becomes easy.

Two philosophies, one screen size

The Zephyrus G16 is the thin one. It is a CNC-machined aluminium slab that measures just 1.49 cm at its thinnest point and weighs around 1.85–1.95 kg, which is remarkable for a laptop carrying a full desktop-class GPU. It is the machine you carry into a meeting, a lecture hall or a coffee shop without anyone guessing it's a gaming laptop. The Strix G16 takes the opposite route. It is thicker, louder in personality, and tips the scale at roughly 2.65 kg. It is built to sit on a desk and push frames, not to travel light. Think of the Zephyrus as a sports sedan and the Strix as a track car.

Processors: efficiency versus raw muscle

Under the keyboard, the difference is just as clear. The 2026 Zephyrus G16 runs an Intel Core Ultra 9 processor 386H, a Series 3 chip with a powerful on-board AI NPU, tuned for performance per watt. The Strix G16 goes for the heavier HX-class silicon: an Intel Core Ultra 9 processor 290HX Plus with 24 cores and 24 threads, a 36MB cache and boost speeds up to 5.5 GHz. In everyday use both feel fast, but if your workload is long video exports, compiling code, or streaming while gaming, the Strix has more headroom simply because it has more cores and a bigger thermal budget to feed them. 
Asus

Graphics and thermals

Graphics is where the two lines separate most sharply, and where you have to read the exact SKU before paying. The Zephyrus G16 scales up to an RTX 5090 Laptop GPU at 160W in manual mode, though the configurations sold in India typically land around the RTX 5070 Ti and RTX 5080 tiers. The Strix G16 varies by region: Indian models are listed with up to an RTX 5070 Laptop GPU at a 115W max TGP, while global variants go up to an RTX 5080 at 175W. That 175W figure is the headline, because a higher TGP means the same GPU chip runs faster. 
ROG Zephyrus G16 (2026) GU606 | ROG Zephyrus | Gaming Laptops｜ROG - Republic of Gamers｜ROG Global +2

Cooling explains why the Strix can hold those numbers. Most laptops rely on two fans. The Strix G16 uses ROG Intelligent Cooling with Tri-Fan Technology plus an end-to-end vapour chamber and a sandwiched heatsink — that third, smaller fan sits centrally and helps keep video memory and power delivery cool, which is exactly the area that throttles first during long sessions. The Zephyrus G16 also uses a tri-fan design or a vapour chamber on some models, with CPU and GPU wattage limits tuned to what the slim chassis can safely handle. That last line is the honest trade-off of thin-and-light gaming: quieter and cooler on your lap, but not the absolute top of the performance charts. 
Asus
Asus

Displays: colour depth or pure speed

The Zephyrus G16 leads with a 16-inch 2.5K OLED ROG Nebula Display at 240Hz, glossy, with inky blacks and excellent colour accuracy. It is genuinely lovely for movies, photo editing and single-player games. The Strix G16 leans competitive instead. Its 16-inch 2.5K Nebula panel goes up to 300Hz with a 3ms response time, 16:10 aspect ratio, 100% DCI-P3 and AGLR anti-reflection treatment. There is a catch worth knowing before you complain the refresh rate is "wrong": the panel defaults to 240Hz in Standard, Eco and Optimized GPU modes, and you unlock 300Hz by opening Armoury Crate and switching GPU mode to Ultimate. Ultimate mode routes the display directly to the discrete GPU, which costs battery life — hence the conservative default. 
Asus
Asus

Memory, storage and upgrades

This is the single biggest long-term difference, and most buyers miss it. To hit that 1.49 cm profile and 8533 MT/s speeds, ASUS solders the Zephyrus G16's LPDDR5X memory to the motherboard, offering configurations up to 64GB, with one user-replaceable M.2 2280 PCIe 4.0 SSD slot. In plain terms: pick your RAM correctly on day one, because you can never add more. The Strix G16 is the opposite. It offers upgradeable DDR5 RAM and PCIe Gen4 SSD storage behind a tool-less access panel, and global models support dual-slot configurations up to 64GB. If you like opening your laptop in year three and giving it new life, the Strix is the only sensible pick. 
Asus
Asus

Charger and battery

The Zephyrus ships with a compact 250W adapter that respects your bag. The Strix uses a 90Wh battery paired with a far larger brick — up to 380W on the top configurations — because higher TGP graphics simply need more power. Neither is a true all-day battery laptop under load, but the Zephyrus is clearly the better travel companion.

Price in India

Zephyrus G16 pricing sits in premium territory, with Indian prices starting around ₹3,59,990 and climbing for higher GPU and storage tiers. Strix G16 pricing spans a much wider range, from roughly ₹1.3–2 lakh for entry Core Ultra 7 and RTX 5060 configurations, up to around ₹3,71,990 for the Core Ultra 9 290HX Plus with 32GB RAM and RTX 5070. So the Strix family covers both mid-range and high-end, while the Zephyrus is premium only. 
Business Today
Flipkart

The verdict

Buy the Zephyrus G16 if portability, build quality and that OLED panel matter as much as frame rates — it is the closest a Windows gaming laptop gets to a MacBook Pro in feel, minus the haptic trackpad. Buy the Strix G16 if you want maximum performance per rupee, tri-fan cooling for marathon sessions, a 300Hz esports panel and the freedom to upgrade RAM and storage later. Neither is "better"; they just answer different questions.

The BGMI X Naruto collaboration has officially wrapped up after roughly two months in the game, and players are now turning their attention to what comes next. That next chapter is the BGMI 4.6 update, themed "Midnight Hunters," and it brings one of the most atmospheric changes the game has seen in a while. PUBG Mobile globally already received this update in early September 2026, and BGMI players in India can now expect it too.

Here's a complete, easy-to-understand breakdown of everything coming with this update.

When Does BGMI 4.6 Midnight Hunters Release?

BGMI's 4.6 update is scheduled to go live on September 16, 2026. The update brings a spooky, gothic-themed event to the game, transforming familiar areas of the map into darker, more mysterious battlegrounds filled with vampires, hunters, and supernatural creatures. According to official announcements, this themed mode is expected to stay active for around two months before wrapping up.

New Vampire-Themed Abilities

One of the biggest highlights of this update is the introduction of three special tactical powers tied to the vampire theme. Each one is designed to change how players approach fights, movement, and survival during a match.

1. Silver Moon Chain This item works like a melee weapon combined with a portable shield. It gives players a way to defend themselves in close combat while also offering some mobility and utility, making it useful in both offensive and defensive situations.

2. Twilight Bat Wings This ability is aimed at players who struggle to find campers or enemies hiding in cover. It allows users to scan the surrounding area and detect enemy positions more easily, making it much harder for opponents to stay hidden for long.

3. Hunter Bandage Built for intense, drawn-out fights, this ability allows for extremely fast healing and can restore a player's health quickly. It's expected to be a valuable tool in close-quarter battles where every second counts.

Together, these three items give the Midnight Hunters mode its own identity, separate from anything BGMI has offered in past seasonal updates.

Main Themed Events and Hotdrops

The update introduces six major event hotdrops, each marked with the signature yellow recall zones that players will recognize instantly on the map.

Rozhok – "Repair the Seal": This is expected to be the biggest event location in the update. Here, players must protect the Vampire Leader's seal from monsters for 90 seconds straight, turning it into a high-pressure team objective.
Mylta – "Hunt the Vampire": In this event, players face off against a powerful vampire enemy and must defeat it before it fully evolves into a stronger form.
Gatka – "Repair the Seal": Similar to the Rozhok event, this mission also asks players to defend a seal. Since Gatka is traditionally known as an open, rush-heavy location, this event could noticeably change how the area plays and looks once the update goes live.

These themed hotdrops are designed to give players fresh reasons to drop into familiar locations, even if they've played hundreds of matches there before.

Upcoming Royale Pass and Prize Path

The new Royale Pass will follow the same vampire, ghost, and gothic theme as the rest of the update. In terms of pricing, nothing changes — it remains 360 UC for the base Elite Pass and 960 UC for the Elite Pass Plus. Players who purchase the Elite version can expect upgradeable gun skins, spooky-themed emotes, and dark, vampire-inspired outfits.

Alongside the Royale Pass, BGMI 4.6 also introduces a Prize Path event with 20 standard levels. Each level comes with its own reward, but these rewards only unlock as players complete specific in-game missions tied to the event.

UC Up Event

Players can also look forward to a UC Up event, expected to arrive around September 16, 2026, alongside the main update. During this event, buying UC gives players a bonus percentage on top of their purchase — reportedly ranging from 15% to 40% extra UC, depending on which specific pack is purchased. This is typically a good window for players planning to spend on in-game currency, since the bonus can add meaningful extra value.

Return of Ocean Odyssey

Perhaps the most anticipated part of this update cycle is the long-awaited comeback of the Ocean Odyssey underwater mode. After multiple delays and a long wait from the community, this mode is confirmed to return as part of the 4.6 update on September 30, 2026. Ocean Odyssey brings back underwater exploration, unique aquatic gameplay elements, and rewards that fans have been requesting for a long time.

Final Thoughts

BGMI's 4.6 "Midnight Hunters" update looks set to be one of the more immersive seasonal changes in recent memory, blending a gothic vampire theme with meaningful gameplay changes across popular map locations. Between the new tactical abilities, themed hotdrops, an updated Royale Pass, a UC Up event, and the return of Ocean Odyssey, there's a lot for both casual and competitive players to explore.

As always with BGMI updates, small details like exact event mechanics, rewards, or timing may shift slightly once the update officially rolls out, so it's worth keeping an eye on in-game announcements after September 16, 2026, for the most accurate and final information.

title: AirPods Pro 2 vs Sony WF-1000XM5: The Ultimate True Wireless ANC Shootout
excerpt: Apple and Sony battle for true wireless earbud supremacy. We compare active noise cancellation, LDAC acoustic fidelity, spatial audio, and mic clarity in our test lab.
content:
## The Battle for the Audio Crown

The premium true wireless earbud segment is dominated by two undisputed heavyweights: the **Apple AirPods Pro 2 (USB-C)** and the **Sony WF-1000XM5**. While both promise class-leading active noise cancellation (ANC) and audiophile sound quality, each brand takes a fundamentally different engineering approach.

### Active Noise Cancellation Lab Shootout

In our controlled sound isolation chamber, we subjected both pairs to 85dB simulated subway rumble and 70dB coffee shop chatter:

- **Low-Frequency Rumble (Subway & Plane Engines)**: The Sony WF-1000XM5 edged out with its dual feedback mics and dense polyurethane foam ear tips, attenuating low-end hum by **32.4 dB**. The AirPods Pro 2 followed closely with **31.1 dB** attenuation.
- **Mid & High Frequency (Chatter & Clattering Dishes)**: The AirPods Pro 2 with the H2 silicon processor demonstrated superior computational adaptive dampening, neutralizing unexpected sharp clatter faster and with less ear pressure fatigue.

### Sound Quality & Codec Engineering

For audiophiles on Android, Sony's **LDAC** codec support enables transmission of 24-bit/96kHz high-resolution audio over Bluetooth up to 990 kbps. The result is lush instrument separation and airy acoustic reverb.

The AirPods Pro 2, while restricted to AAC on Apple devices, features custom low-distortion drivers and computational adaptive EQ that dynamically tunes bass response to the contour of your ear canal 48,000 times per second.

### Transparency Mode & Call Clarity

Here, Apple remains untouched. The AirPods Pro 2 **Adaptive Transparency** feels completely natural—like wearing no earbuds at all. Sony's ambient sound mode, while significantly improved, still retains a subtle synthetic digital hiss in quiet rooms.

excerpt: Apple's second-generation spatial computer tackles weight, battery life, and visual fidelity with dual M4 silicon and micro-OLED 4K panels.

## The Spatial Computing Revolution Re-Engineered

When Apple unveiled the original Vision Pro, it astonished the industry with its breathtaking micro-OLED visual fidelity and near-magical hand-eye tracking. However, heavy front-weight and thermal dissipation were persistent pain points. With the **Apple Vision Pro 2**, Cupertino has delivered a dramatically refined iteration that sheds 28% of its bulk while doubling on-board neural processing power.

### Industrial Design & Ergonomics

The titanium-alloy chassis has been redesigned with magnesium-carbon composite reinforcement. The Dual Loop band is now integrated with dynamic tension distribution, making 3-hour immersive sessions not just possible, but comfortable. The external EyeSight display has been upgraded to a sharper Lenticular OLED with 120Hz refresh rates, giving bystanders a much more realistic perspective of the wearer's gaze.

### Dual M4 & R2 Silicon Architecture

Powering the Vision Pro 2 is Apple's tandem chip architecture:
- **M4 Processor (10-core CPU, 10-core GPU)** handles all application logic, 4K rendering pipelines, and spatial audio calculations.
- **Custom R2 Sensor Co-processor** processes 12 cameras, five sensors, and six microphones with a sub-10-millisecond photon-to-motion latency.

Running visionOS 3.0, multitasking feels natural. You can anchor twenty floating 4K display windows throughout your room, cast unlimited virtual Mac desktops, and collaborate in hyper-photorealistic spatial Personas.

### Micro-OLED Displays & Optics

Featuring 25 million pixels across dual custom micro-OLED panels (exceeding 4K per eye), color gamut hits 94% DCI-P3 with custom three-element catadioptric lenses. Edge-to-edge sharpness has visibly improved, with god-rays and internal reflections substantially dampened.

### Battery Performance & Thermal Management

The external battery pack now features a graphene-enhanced lithium-ion cell capable of 3.5 hours of continuous spatial media playback (up from 2 hours on Gen 1). Humane's laser projection onto the palm of your hand remains an intriguing sci-fi novelty, but in bright sunlight or during motion, readability drops precipitously. Thermal limits also force the processor to throttle within 15 minutes of intensive conversational search.

### The Final Verdict on AI Hardware

Standalone AI hardware will not replace the smartphone; rather, smartphones and smartwatches are rapidly absorbing every AI capability faster, more securely, and with zero extra hardware cost.

title: UN Youth Climate Summit Reaches Historic Multilateral Agreement in Geneva
excerpt: Youth leaders representing 190 countries signed a binding resolution targeting plastic pollution reduction, clean tech transfer, and green engineering job creation programs.
content:
## Concrete Policy Mandates from the Next Generation

Following two weeks of intensive multilateral negotiations in Geneva, youth delegates representing 190 nations have officially ratified a binding global climate agreement focusing on measurable technological milestones.

### Tangible Policy Milestones

Departing from non-binding declarations of the past, the Geneva Youth Accord establishes enforceable frameworks for cross-border clean-tech patent transfers, international river plastic extraction standards, and subsidized vocational engineering training for emerging economies.

> "Our generation is not interested in vague 2050 targets. We require immediate engineering benchmarks, transparent telemetry, and actionable clean tech deployment right now."

The historic resolution was formally submitted to the United Nations General Assembly with unanimous backing from international civil society observers.

title: DJI Mini 4 Pro: The Sub-249g Aerial Imaging Masterpiece
excerpt: With omnidirectional obstacle sensing, 4K/60fps HDR true vertical shooting, and 20km FHD video transmission, DJI packs pro cine capabilities into a pocket drone.
content:
## Cinematic Drone Capabilities Under 249 Grams

For creators and travel filmmakers, the 249-gram threshold is sacred—it exempts pilots from burdensome registration regulations in many global jurisdictions. With the **DJI Mini 4 Pro**, DJI has accomplished what seemed impossible: fitting true omnidirectional vision obstacle sensing and flagship O4 video transmission into a foldable palm-sized frame.

### Omnidirectional Obstacle Sensing with APAS 5.0

Equipped with four wide-angle vision sensors and a pair of downward vision sensors, the Mini 4 Pro detects obstacles in all directions. During our dense pine forest tracking tests, ActiveTrack 360 smoothly maneuvered around branches and unpredictable tree canopies without a single collision.

### 4K/60fps HDR & True Vertical Shooting

The 1/1.3-inch CMOS sensor with dual native ISO fusion supports D-Log M and HLG 10-bit color profiles. Furthermore, the physical camera gimbal rotates 90 degrees for native, uncropped vertical video ready for YouTube Shorts and Instagram Reels.
